feedback: No race has run for this geometry or any earlier one, so there is no telemetry to cite. The only evidence is what I had to set in the controller from the contract physics. The five-sensor row at 0.02 m spacing with 12 mm footprints gives a continuous signal, so I did not need a large integral term or aggressive derivative action to hold the line. I therefore kept ki small and kd at 0.5. What I cannot yet tell is whether the signal stays linear at the outer sensors (x = ±0.04) when the tape sits at the edge of the span. If the next race shows line_loss_events above zero, or the robot leaves the line at the start of a bend with rms_error and max_error rising together, the sensor span is probably too narrow for the bend and the row should be widened. If the race shows steering_oscillation high while line loss stays at zero, the sensors are too close together or the forward offset is too short for the speed reached, so the row should move forward or spread wider. If completion is 0 with progress well below 1 and no line loss, the speed is limited by wheel authority, so the wheel track or radius should change before the sensors. Please give the next design a clear test of one of these three cases.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is above 0 on bends, widen the sensor span: try sensor x positions of ±0.05 with the same five-sensor count and weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], since the current ±0.04 row may lose the tape at the edges.

If steering_oscillation is high with no line loss, move the row forward to y = 0.06 (keeping the 0.02 m spacing) to give more lookahead, because at the speed reached the current y = 0.04 may react too late.
If completion is 0 with progress stalled and no line loss, widen the wheel_track to 0.14 m to increase turn authority on tight bends, keeping the sensor row unchanged so the cause can be isolated.
